column1: # BORU Language Specification: Patrun — pattern→value dispatch tables
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `patrun T` builds a mutable Patrun (vendored github.com/rjrodger/patrun)
# whose every stored/matched value is DECLARED to be a T. `add {pattern}
# value pm` registers a rule (in place, value must be a T); `find {subject}
# pm` returns the value of the MOST SPECIFIC pattern that subset-matches the
# subject — more matched keys win, unknown subject keys are ignored — as
# `T | None` (a miss reads None). Match-values in the PATTERN are Scalars
# compared by STRING COERCION (1 and "1" share a rule; 1.0 and true key on
# their own text). `add` / `remove` fold a Patrun overload into the core
# words; the receiver type disambiguates, so `add 1 2` stays arithmetic.
# §1  specificity + subset matching
def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  add {a:1 b:1} "B" r  add {a:1 b:2} "C" r  find {a:1} r
column3: the least specific rule

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  add {a:1 b:1} "B" r  add {a:1 b:2} "C" r  find {a:1 b:1} r
column3: more matched keys win

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  add {a:1 b:1} "B" r  add {a:1 b:2} "C" r  find {a:1 b:2} r
column3: a different value on b selects C

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  find {a:1 z:9} r
column3: an unknown subject key is ignored (subset match)

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  find {x:9} r
column3: no matching rule → None

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {} "D" r  add {a:1} "A" r  find {x:9} r
column3: the empty pattern is the catch-all default

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {} "D" r  add {a:1} "A" r  find {a:1} r
column3: a specific rule beats the default

column1: # §2  scalar match-values, compared by string coercion
def r (patrun String)  add {n:1} "int" r  find {n:1} r
column3: integer match

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {n:1} "int" r  find {n:"1"} r
column3: coercion: integer 1 and string "1" share a rule

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {n:1} "int" r  find {n:1.0} r
column3: 1.0 coerces to "1.0", distinct from "1"

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {flag:true} "on" r  find {flag:true} r
column3: booleans coerce to "true"/"false"

column1: # §3  tie-break (specificity equal) + overwrite
def r (patrun String)  add {a:1 b:1} "X" r  add {a:1 c:1} "Y" r  find {a:1 b:1 c:1} r
column3: equal key counts: alphabetically earlier ({a,b} < {a,c}) wins

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  add {a:1} "A2" r  find {a:1} r
column3: re-adding the same pattern overwrites its value

column1: # §4  exact / remove / patterns
def r (patrun String)  add {a:1 b:1} "B" r  find {a:1} r {exact:true}
column3: exact: a partial (subset) match does not count

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1 b:1} "B" r  find {a:1 b:1} r {exact:true}
column3: exact: identical key set matches

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  remove {a:1} r  find {a:1} r
column3: remove deletes a rule by its pattern

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  add {b:2} "B" r  patterns r
column3: patterns lists the rules in registration order

column1: # §5  dispatch (values are functions), truthiness, typeof
def api (patrun Function)  add {cmd:"sum"} ([m:Map] => [m.x add m.y]) api  def h (find {cmd:"sum" x:3 y:4} api)  h {x:3 y:4}
column3: the matched value is a handler function, then called

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  if (find {a:1} r) ["Y"] ["N"]
column3: a found value is truthy

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  if (find {x:9} r) ["Y"] ["N"]
column3: None is falsy → the else branch

column1: typeof (patrun String)
column3: the type of a Patrun

column1: # §6  add stays polymorphic — the receiver type disambiguates
add 1 2
column3: integer add is untouched
float add is untouched

column1: # §7  negatives
def r (patrun String)  add {a:[1 2]} "X" r
column3: a non-scalar pattern value is rejected (unlike patrun-JS stringification)

column1: def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} 5 r
column3: the stored value must be the declared type (5 is an Integer, not a String)

column1: find {a:1} {b:2}
column3: find needs a Patrun receiver, not a plain Map

column1: add {a:1} "v" 5
column3: the 3-arg add requires a Patrun receiver (5 is an Integer)
